research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9942 at 13 FR 1823 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 1, 1948; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 3, 1948 issue. The register title is Providing for the Performance of Certain Functions Under the Rubber Act of 1948.  Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 734 to 2164 of the held text, from the authority recital through paragraph 4 and its effective date. The dossier splits the order into a lead clause, paragraphs 1 to 4 and a separate fragment holding only the year of the effective date ("1948."), which is not a command. Content: paragraph 1 has the Secretary of Commerce perform the functions the President holds under sections 3, 4, 18(c) and 18(d) of the Rubber Act of 1948; paragraph 2 has the Reconstruction Finance Corporation perform those under sections 5(c), 5(e), 6, 7, 8, 11(a) and 18(f), with a proviso about section 6(a); paragraph 3 divides the functions under sections 10 and 12 between them; paragraph 4 makes the order effective April 1, 1948. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9942 describes providing for performance of functions under the Rubber Act of 1948). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Later event: Executive Order 10539 of June 22, 1954 (held text, section 2) amends this order by deleting from sections 2 and 3 the words "Reconstruction Finance Corporation" and inserting in each case the words "Federal Facilities Corporation." Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments it is a later event, not an end; the order continued, as amended, until the revocation. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain no end date or termination clause; paragraph 4 sets the effective date. The dossier chain names Executive Order 10539 (amendment) and Executive Order 12553 (revocation). The Rubber Act of 1948 is not held in the packet, so whether the statute's own expiry or later rubber-facility disposal legislation ended these functions before 1986 cannot be checked, and no end is claimed on that ground. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.
